hints: Look first at the top split in the diagram, short term versus long term. Ask yourself, in which case are antibodies just borrowed, and in which case does the body make its own?

Remember the two separate decisions: active means you make your own antibodies and memory cells, passive means you receive ready-made antibodies. Natural means no human medical intervention, artificial means by injection.
walkthrough:
**Decide what 1 means from short term**

Both examples under 1 involve receiving ready-made antibodies, either across the placenta or by injection into the blood. You do not make them yourself, so there is no memory and protection is short term.

Rule: received antibodies = passive immunity.

**Decide what long term means**

Both examples under long term involve exposure to antigen, either by real infection or by attenuated pathogen in a vaccine. Your own B and T lymphocytes respond and make memory cells, so protection is long term.

Rule: own response + memory = active immunity.

**Split natural versus artificial**

Natural means it happens without medical help. Infection by a pathogen (2) and antibodies across the placenta are natural. Artificial means humans intervene by injection. Injection of antibodies and injection of attenuated pathogen as vaccine (3) are artificial.

So 1 = passive, 2 = natural active, 3 = artificial active. That matches row D.

options.A: Incorrect because 1 is not active. Receiving antibodies gives no memory cells, so it is passive, short term immunity.
options.B: Incorrect because 1 is not active. Short term borrowed antibodies always means passive, not active.
options.C: Incorrect because 2 and 3 are swapped. Infection is natural, while injection of attenuated pathogen (vaccination) is artificial.
options.D: Correct. 1 is passive (ready-made antibodies given), 2 is natural active (real infection), 3 is artificial active (vaccine).
